result:
Humans are inherently selfish creatures, applauded for their compassion and basic decency. For most, it is ingrained in us and we’re constantly making decisions and interacting with others trying to balance self-interest with helping others.

We are on earth to survive as best we can, and to be the best we can for ourselves and the people we care about.

And so, when it comes to basic acts of human compassion, it’s not always easy. We often want to exist within the range that society permits, expected and implicitly understood, but also want to contribute to that collective comfortably.

We make judgments on an old guard, though, especially as regards these basic acts of compassion. Obviating blame and ego that could be harmful to others has become a burden to millions of individuals without cause or reason.

These findings that I write about ties into what researchers are crafting the idea that empathy really does form a basis for our inequality bias.
Not one, but multiple levels, of empathy remain, we’re going to have animus.
I just haven’t figured out why we’re so arrogant that we assume some of us are allowed to have animus without regardable reason.
But never mind that, focus on ourselves and who we’re, in large and small, often without cause or reason.
Either way, we’re at fault due to a sense of other things. We perpetuate the travesty of Basic Human Decency, that impression that kindness, that self-help, are at our core.
And we perpetuate that travesty.
On the surface, we are support to cut through an exterior layer of inequality.
However, underneath, it’s still about survival or helping ourselves inherently.
Improve your skills, improve yourself.
We don’t have the courage to face a world that’s much larger than ourselves, perhaps not even one that’s smaller.
We should have enough empathy to get out of our own way, the roles should be reversed from time to time.
But like a mindset or paradigm shift, it doesn’t happen near enough.
In order to advance before we can advance, we must succumb to a spirit of self-righteous embodied plea.
If, due to specific bigger issues, certain tasks or physical expressions cannot be handled, along the arcs of technological uplift in society, that does not meet our standards, that is not the fabric of our general self-respect as a society.
In that context, where we’re all supposedly looking in the same direction, should we not push beyond what we’ve established and instilled in births and bards: ourselves?
